gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa reads as a plain sans with open curves and clear gaps, its lowercase filling most of the line height. Woodgod is the one that throws its weight around, while the body font simply makes every letter easy to find.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Woodgod pours a wide channel into every bowl, and its lowercase climbs nearly to the capitals. Then Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its strokes out before they touch, so the pair is mostly a study in loud versus hushed.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Commanding and a bit vintage up top, Woodgod hands off to a body whose lowercase crowds toward the capital line. Noto Sans Tai Tham keeps its c wide open, which is the quiet part.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Noto Sans Tai Viet reads with short ascenders and a tall x-height, its terminals pulled back from where each curve would close. Give that sans a modest size and Woodgod can handle the loud part.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-takri: Contemporary in feel, Noto Sans Takri leaves every small round letter generously unclosed, sitting on a high-waisted lowercase. But Woodgod is the one built to command attention, with its vintage swagger, while the body font just keeps the text moving.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Woodgod looks vintage and commanding, with a wide channel running into every bowl. Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified even at ordinary size, so shrinking the heading or enlarging the body would blur the difference between them.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tamil-su: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement looks stocky, with rounds like open parentheses. Over a full page, its tall middle band keeps lines dense and sturdy, which gives Woodgod's vintage, commanding headings something solid to sit over.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Tall lowercase that nearly touches the capitals is what stands out about Woodgod, and it gives the pair its vintage bite. Noto Sans Tangsa takes the gentler job, with wide, inviting round letters and short ascender stems.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC has large open counters in its tall a, e and s, and its curves open outward rather than curling in. Woodgod commands attention with vintage weight, while this body font stays approachable.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Woodgod's tall lowercase nearly reaches its capitals. Noto Sans Telugu then sets a high midline with counters connected to the outside, so a long page feels professional and unfussy.
